claims.text: A machine-learning model using high-dimensional atomic-mass, bonding, and lattice-dynamics descriptors can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The machine-learning approach will improve prediction accuracy by at least 20% relative to traditional rule-based or semi-empirical methods.
The target high-entropy alloys have diverse atomic compositions and random solid-solution structures.
The proposed model is to be trained on experimentally measured phonon thermal conductivities of high-entropy alloys.
Atomic mass variance, bond stiffness, and lattice anharmonicity are proposed as predictive features.
Reliable application requires a dataset spanning a wide range of high-entropy-alloy compositions and structures.
The model must be evaluated using cross-validation.
Random solid-solution structures introduce atomic-scale disorder.
Atomic-scale disorder in random solid solutions affects phonon scattering.
Machine learning can capture complex, nonlinear relationships between atomic-scale features and phonon thermal conductivity.
Traditional predictive methods do not easily account for these complex, nonlinear relationships.
MAE and RMSE can be used to compare the predictive performance of the machine-learning and traditional methods.
The approach is applicable to high-entropy alloys having random solid-solution structures.
The approach is not intended to cover materials with significant secondary phases or non-random microstructures.
The expected performance depends on the training dataset being sufficiently large and diverse to represent the relevant features of high-entropy alloys.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% improvement over traditional methods on a separate test set would falsify the hypothesis.
